entries.summary: We are excited to announce PHP Conference Kansai 2026! 🎉 About the conference PHP Conference Kansai is a technical conference where PHP engineers in the Kansai region of Japan share their knowledge and experience.
entries.text: We are excited to announce PHP Conference Kansai 2026! 🎉 About the conference PHP Conference Kansai is a technical conference where PHP engineers in the Kansai region of Japan share their knowledge and experience. It started in 2011 and came back in 2024 in Osaka after a six-year break. It was held in Kobe in 2025, and this edition will be held in Kyoto. The theme of this edition is "次は、ここから始まる。" (What's next starts here.) AI has dramatically changed the way we work. But the quality of the answers you get from AI depends on how much you know when you ask. To ask the right questions and judge whether an answer holds up, you need to learn from others and see beyond your own perspective. At the conference, through sessions, talks, and casual conversations around the venue, you can talk with people who have a shared knowledge base. We want it to be a place where everyone who comes finds their own "next." Note: Despite its name, the conference takes place in January 2027. Who can join? Anyone involved with PHP is welcome, whether you use it now, used it before, or are just curious about it. (All talks will be in Japanese.) Basic facts Date: January 16, 2027 (JST) Location: Kyoto Research Park, Building 4, Kyoto, Japan Timetable Tickets For more information, see the event page: PHP Conference Kansai 2026. Follow us on X (Twitter).
entries.title: PHP Conference Kansai 2026 (JAPAN)

entries.summary: The PHP development team announces the immediate availability of PHP 8.6.0. This release marks a major update to the PHP language.
entries.text: The PHP development team announces the immediate availability of PHP 8.6.0. This release marks a major update to the PHP language. PHP 8.6 comes with numerous improvements and new features such as: Partial Function Application Default values for readonly properties New Io\Poll API for monitoring streams New clamp() function New \Time\Duration class New SortDirection enum See what’s new in PHP 8.6 for more highlights and examples. Source downloads for PHP 8.6.0 are available on our downloads page. Windows source and binaries are available on the Windows downloads page. The list of changes is recorded in the ChangeLog. The migration guide in the PHP Manual lists new features and backward-incompatible changes in detail. Kudos to all the contributors and supporters!

entries.summary: The PHP security team announces upcoming security releases scheduled for Thursday, 19 November 2026, between 14:00 and 14:30 UTC.
entries.text: The PHP security team announces upcoming security releases scheduled for Thursday, 19 November 2026, between 14:00 and 14:30 UTC. These releases are part of PHP’s regular four-week release cycle and will address security vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions. The highest severity is CRITICAL. The issues rated CRITICAL require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups. Users are strongly encouraged to prepare to upgrade promptly once the releases become available. Technical details and fixed version numbers will be published alongside the releases. Thank you for helping us keep PHP secure.

entries.summary: The PHP team announces updated Windows builds: PHP 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1. These builds include Brotli 1.2.1, which fixes CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Brotli decompression.
entries.text: The PHP team announces updated Windows builds: PHP 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1. These builds include Brotli 1.2.1, which fixes CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Brotli decompression. In PHP Windows builds, the vulnerable decoder can be reached through the cURL extension when automatic HTTP response decompression is enabled. This is disabled by default in cURL, but applications and HTTP client libraries can enable it. The -1 suffix identifies a Windows package rebuild with updated dependencies. These builds use the same PHP source releases, and the PHP runtime versions remain unchanged. The updated packages are available on the downloads page.
entries.title: Updated PHP Windows builds for Brotli security fix

entries.summary: We suggest you set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector.
entries.text: We suggest you set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector. This setting was already listed as a mitigation in the GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp advisory for CVE-2026-109619 published on Oct 21st, 2026. If you applied it then, keep it in place and no further action is needed. The issue can only occur under an unusual combination of configuration and application code. An application must set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start(). Session upload progress must also still be enabled. Applications that never change the serialize handler at runtime can keep the feature enabled. Since this setup is unlikely in practice, we are handling it in the regular release cycle and will publish a full advisory for CVE-2026-115560 with the next release.
entries.title: Informational advisory: Session upload progress

entries.summary: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution.
entries.text: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately. Who is at risk: all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs. The vulnerabilities: RCE via OOM corruption, CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w): out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid. RCE via stale global state, CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp): request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it. How to update: Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Source downloads are on our downloads page. Windows source and binaries are on the same page. Linux distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance, so check your vendor for updated packages. PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project. Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor for details, or upgrade to a supported version. Given the severity of these vulnerabilities, the PHP
entries.title: Security advisory: Critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, update now

entries.summary: The State of PHP survey is still open, but not for much longer. It asks how PHP is working for you: what you build with, what is painful, and what you think PHP should focus on next.
entries.text: The State of PHP survey is still open, but not for much longer. It asks how PHP is working for you: what you build with, what is painful, and what you think PHP should focus on next. It takes around 15 minutes. The survey is run by The PHP Foundation in partnership with PhpStorm by JetBrains. The aggregated results will be published later this year as the State of PHP 2026 report. The anonymized raw dataset will be released along with it, so anyone in the community can check the numbers or run their own analysis. More responses mean a better picture of what matters to PHP users. If you have not filled it in yet, please do, and share it with your colleagues and user groups.
entries.title: Last Call for the State of PHP Survey

entries.summary: The PHP team is pleased to announce the second testing release of PHP 8.6.0, Alpha 3. This continues the PHP 8.6 release cycle, the rough outline of which is specified in the PHP Wiki.
entries.text: The PHP team is pleased to announce the second testing release of PHP 8.6.0, Alpha 3. This continues the PHP 8.6 release cycle, the rough outline of which is specified in the PHP Wiki. For source downloads of PHP 8.6.0 Alpha 3 please visit the download page. Please carefully test this version and report any issues found in the GitHub Issues. Please DO NOT use this version in production, it is an early test version. For more information on the new features and other changes, you can read the NEWS file, or the UPGRADING file for a complete list of upgrading notes. These files can also be found in the release archive. The next release will be Beta 1, planned for 13 August 2026. The signatures for the release can be found in the manifest or on the pre-release builds page. Thank you for helping us make PHP better.
entries.title: PHP 8.6.0 Alpha 3 available for testing

entries.summary: The International PHP Conference is the world's first PHP conference and has stood for more than two decades for top-notch pragmatic expertise in PHP and web technologies.
entries.text: The International PHP Conference is the world's first PHP conference and has stood for more than two decades for top-notch pragmatic expertise in PHP and web technologies. At the IPC, internationally renowned experts from the PHP industry meet up with PHP users and developers from large and small companies. Here is the place where concepts emerge and ideas are born – the IPC signifies knowledge transfer at the highest level. Basic facts: Date: October 26 – 30, 2026 Location: Holiday Inn Munich City Centre, Munich or Online Highlights: 60+ best practice sessions 50+ international top speakers PHPower: Hands-on Power Workshops 2-Day Bootcamp on Thursday and Friday Expo with exciting exhibitors on October 27 & 28 All inclusive: Changing buffets, snacks & refreshing drinks Official certificate for attendees Free Goodies: Developer bag, T-Shirt, magazines etc. Exclusive networking events For further information on the International PHP Conference Munich visit: https://phpconference.com/munich/
entries.title: International PHP Conference Munich 2026

entries.summary: Join us for the 19th Annual Web Developer Conference, PHP Tek 2027, April 27-29 2026. PHP Tek combines leadership, expertise, and networking in one event.
entries.text: Join us for the 19th Annual Web Developer Conference, PHP Tek 2027, April 27-29 2026. PHP Tek combines leadership, expertise, and networking in one event. A relaxing atmosphere for tech leaders and developers to share, learn and grow professionally while also providing you with the knowledge to solve your everyday problems. We are the longest-running web developer conference in the United States, focusing on the PHP programming language. The event is broken up into multiple days. The main conference happens over the course of 3 days (April 27-29) and includes keynotes, talks, and networking options. It will be broken into three tracks and will cover a range of topics. There will be two dedicated PHP Tracks, and then each day will have a different 3rd track (JS/Laravel/DevOps) Head over to https://phptek.io and get yours today!
entries.title: PHP Tek 2027
